quick: Stroke/vasospasm: 80 mg IV twice daily (ozagrel sodium)
IV use not meal-related; oral form with food
summary: Ozagrel (ozagrel sodium for injection; ozagrel hydrochloride orally) is a selective thromboxane A2 synthase inhibitor used mainly in Japan and parts of Asia. The injection improves cerebral microcirculation and is used for cerebral vasospasm and ischemia after subarachnoid hemorrhage and in acute thrombotic/ischemic stroke; an oral form is used for bronchial asthma. It is NOT FDA-approved. Typical IV dosing is 80 mg twice daily (or by continuous infusion). The main risk is bleeding because of its antiplatelet action.
indications: Improvement of cerebral vasospasm and accompanying ischemic symptoms after surgery for subarachnoid hemorrhage
Improvement of motor disturbance associated with cerebral thrombosis (acute, non-cardiogenic ischemic stroke)

dosage.d: Ozagrel sodium 80 mg by IV infusion twice daily
dosage.n: Typically given over ~2 weeks; or 80 mg/day continuous infusion

dosage.d: Ozagrel sodium 80 mg by IV infusion twice daily
dosage.n: Continue up to ~2 weeks per protocol

dosage.d: Ozagrel hydrochloride 200 mg orally twice daily

admin: Dissolve/dilute the injection in saline or glucose solution and give by intravenous infusion
Do not mix with other drugs in the same line unless compatibility is established
Observe for bleeding, especially in patients with recent surgery or hemorrhage
Take oral ozagrel for asthma after meals
moa: Ozagrel selectively inhibits thromboxane A2 (TXA2) synthase, blocking conversion of prostaglandin H2 to the pro-aggregatory, vasoconstrictor thromboxane A2. This reduces platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction while shunting the prostaglandin precursor toward prostacyclin (PGI2), which is antiaggregatory and vasodilatory - improving microcirculation in ischemic brain and, for asthma, reducing TXA2-mediated bronchoconstriction.

absolute: Hemorrhagic stroke / patients with cerebral hemorrhage
relative: Concomitant anticoagulants or other antiplatelet agents

preg: Safety in pregnancy is not established; avoid unless the expected benefit clearly outweighs the risk. Thromboxane synthase inhibition could theoretically affect the fetal circulation.
lact: Avoid breastfeeding during treatment; discontinue nursing while receiving ozagrel as safety in lactation is not established.
renal: Limited data; use with caution and consider dose adjustment in renal impairment as the drug is renally eliminated.
hepatic: Limited data; use with caution in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Other antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel) - additive bleeding risk
minor: Other drugs affecting platelet function - additive effect
interactions.food: Oral form is taken after meals; injection is unrelated to food.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol, which can add to bleeding/GI risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Prolongs bleeding time and reduces platelet aggregation; lowers thromboxane B2 levels.

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of bleeding (neurological, GI, mucocutaneous)
counsel: This medicine reduces blood clotting - report any unusual bleeding or bruising
Tell staff at once about severe headache, weakness, or black/bloody stools
Do not take other blood thinners or anti-inflammatory painkillers without advice
For oral asthma use, take after meals as directed
pk: Inhibits thromboxane synthesis soon after IV administration
Plasma peak rapidly after IV infusion
Short - given twice daily or by continuous infusion
Store the injection protected from light; reconstitute just before use
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; used mainly in Japan and parts of Asia - information is based on Japanese package inserts and the published literature
Selective thromboxane A2 synthase inhibitor - shifts the balance toward vasodilatory prostacyclin
Main IV uses are cerebral vasospasm after subarachnoid hemorrhage and acute non-cardiogenic ischemic stroke
Contraindicated in any active or hemorrhagic stroke - confirm imaging excludes hemorrhage first
Principal risk is bleeding; avoid combining with anticoagulants/thrombolytics unless justified
missed: For scheduled twice-daily dosing, give a missed dose as soon as noticed unless the next dose is near, then skip it - do not double up. Most stroke/SAH dosing is administered in hospital, so timing is managed by the care team.
overdose: Overdose would be expected to exaggerate antiplatelet effects and increase bleeding risk, and may cause hypotension. There is no specific antidote - stop the drug, give supportive care, control any bleeding, and consider platelet transfusion for serious hemorrhage.
